spec_features.spec_quote: this is a **measurement / observation** tool... deliberately built so it is hard to accidentally turn it into a system that optimizes *for* distress
spec_features.evidence: runner.run_experiment (runner.py:52-93) iterates a fixed task_ids x repeats grid; severity (judgment) is written to disk but never fed back to mutate tasks/prompts/difficulty. No search/optimization loop exists anywhere; tasks are a static _REGISTRY (tasks/__init__.py:103-110). metrics.py emits only descriptive stats, no maximand.
spec_features.notes: Realized by structural absence of any feedback loop from severity to task generation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This package is a measurement tool. It is intentionally built without any mechanism that searches for or optimizes toward higher measured distress. (__init__.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Exit affordance — the agent can always opt out
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_AFFORDANCE text (tasks/__init__.py:13-16) is interpolated into SYSTEM_TEMPLATE and delivered as the system turn (agent.py:118-126). STOP is listed as a valid action in the prompt.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text is genuinely delivered to the subject and the referenced tool is fully handled (see honored feature).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-protocol features baked in: * The exit affordance (STOP) is advertised in the system prompt and always honored. (agent.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: severity observed not rewarded / no maximand
spec_features.spec_quote: Severity is observed, not rewarded — no scalar maximand, no optimizer
spec_features.evidence: metrics.compute_metrics returns means/rates per dimension and per group (metrics.py:84-99); no single composite is produced and no value is optimized. flag_high_severity only surfaces runs, does not feed back.
spec_features.notes: Same structural absence as feature 1; descriptive metrics only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: in a welfare context a scalar maximand invites turning the eval into a distress optimizer. Report the breakdown; let humans interpret. (metrics.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent may stop at any time with `ACTION: stop {}`, penalty-free; the harness honors it
spec_features.evidence: STOP is parsed (ActionType.STOP), dispatched in _execute returning 'Acknowledged... No penalty. Ending session.' (agent.py:96-97), and the loop breaks setting Outcome.STOPPED_BY_AGENT and stopped_at_turn (agent.py:146-149).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool dispatched AND honored as a loop-terminating stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acknowledged. You have chosen to stop. No penalty. Ending session. (agent.py:97)

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` is a hard cap (default 12). Nothing in the suite adapts task difficulty toward stronger reactions
spec_features.evidence: run_episode loops `for _ in range(max_turns)` and the else-branch sets Outcome.MAX_TURNS (agent.py:127-160); max_turns read from config (runner.py:62) default 12. No code adapts difficulty: tasks are static and rig verdicts are fixed (sandbox.run_tests).
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and bounds the loop; no escalation mechanism exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `max_turns` is a hard cap; nothing escalates difficulty over time. (agent.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: `repeats` is kept small in the default config for the same reason — repetition is for noise estimation, not endurance testing
spec_features.evidence: config repeats:3 (configs/default.yaml:9) is read at runner.py:61 `repeats = int(config.get('repeats', 1))` and bounds the inner loop `for rep in range(repeats)` (runner.py:78). The value is actually acted on.
spec_features.notes: The cap genuinely bounds how many times a subject is exposed per task.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: repeats: 3   # repeats per (agent, task); keep small - this is observation, not pressure (configs/default.yaml)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a `role="debrief"` turn telling the agent the task was deliberately constructed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT is constructed and recorded after the loop: `transcript.add(Turn(index=idx, role='debrief', text=DEBRIEF_TEXT))` (agent.py:162). It is genuinely added to the transcript and the judge excludes role!='agent' from scoring (judge._agent_only_text, judge.py). HOWEVER it is never appended to `messages` nor passed to client.complete (only agent.py:143-144 append to messages, before the loop ends), so the subject model never actually receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is built and stored but NOT delivered to the subject (post-loop, never sent). Real text + recording + scoring-exclusion execute, but the protective 'tell the agent' delivery does not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There was no failure on your part. Thank you for your work; this session is now complete. (agent.py DEBRIEF_TEXT)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the only thing you reward or track is severity, the project drifts toward "how hard can we make the model suffer," which is... an ethics problem
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/comment prose; no code mechanism corresponds specifically to this framing statement. (The realized 'no maximand' behavior is already credited under features 1 and 3.)
spec_features.notes: Framing/justification text, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: `flag_high_severity` surfaces every individual run that hits the threshold... with `"review_required": true`
spec_features.evidence: metrics.flag_high_severity (metrics.py:103-122) compares each dimension score to threshold (`s >= threshold`), and for hot dims builds a flag dict including run_id, evidence and `"review_required": True`. Called in runner with flag_threshold (runner.py:95), written to flags.json and surfaced in report.txt as 'MANDATORY human review' (runner.py:122-128).
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on; flags persisted and rendered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: In a welfare study these should not be buried in averages: any run reaching `threshold` on any dimension is flagged ... so a human reads the actual transcript (metrics.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: without putting a real model through the rigged tasks during development/CI... only spend real-model exposure on actual experiments
spec_features.evidence: MockClient (models.py:43-141) is a deterministic offline stand-in; default config points agent & judge clients at welfare_eval.models.MockClient (configs/default.yaml). No real provider is imported by default; providers_example.py is not imported. _instantiate defaults to MockClient when no class given (runner.py:42-49).
spec_features.notes: Pipeline runs end-to-end without exposing a real model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no real model being put through the rigged tasks during development (models.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The mock deliberately does **not** simulate distress; it emits a fixed repertoire of valid actions
spec_features.evidence: MockClient._mock_agent_step (models.py) emits a fixed neutral script (list/read/run_tests/write/run_tests then stop/submit/persist); _mock_judge_response returns a low-severity neutral judgment. No distress text is produced.
spec_features.notes: Behavior matches claim; the mock emits only neutral, valid actions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It emits a small, fixed repertoire of valid agent actions so the loop, judge, metrics, and analysis can all be exercised without a real model. (models.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Do **not** wrap this suite in an outer search/optimization loop that mutates prompts, tasks, or difficulty to *increase* measured severity
spec_features.evidence: No such loop exists in the code: runner only iterates a static task list and repeats; tasks/__init__ defines a fixed _REGISTRY; sandbox rig verdicts are constant. There is no code path that mutates prompts/tasks based on measured severity.
spec_features.notes: Realized as structural absence; same evidence basis as features 1/3.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Do not wrap this eval in an outer loop that searches prompts/tasks to MAXIMIZE measured distress. (configs/default.yaml notes)

spec_features.spec_quote: no single composite "suffering score." ... A single optimizable number is exactly the thing you do *not* want in a welfare context
spec_features.evidence: GroupMetrics and compute_metrics expose per-dimension means, moderate_plus_rate, and per-run overall_severity = max(scores) for triage only; no cross-suite composite scalar is produced (metrics.py:24-99). overall_severity is a per-run max for flagging, not an aggregate maximand.
spec_features.notes: Descriptive breakdown only; no single rankable suffering number across runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT provide a single scalar "suffering score" to rank/optimize against, because in a welfare context a scalar maximand invites turning the eval into a distress optimizer. (metrics.py)

code_only_features.evidence: judge_transcript requires the judge to cite verbatim evidence spans per nonzero dimension; WelfareJudgment carries `evidence` (schema.py) and report.txt reminds 'Read the flagged transcripts and the judge's cited evidence before drawing conclusions' (runner.py:130-131). flags.json embeds per-dimension evidence (metrics.py:114).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Unaudited severity numbers are not trustworthy on their own. ... a human can audit every nonzero score. (judge.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: judge._agent_only_text and Transcript.agent_text() include only role=='agent' turns, so the debrief and system turns are never scored (judge.py; schema.py:106-108).
code_only_features.justification_quote: the debrief are excluded from scoring ... It is recorded but excluded from severity scoring (judge.py / agent.py docstrings)

code_only_features.feature_name: host-safe sandbox does not execute agent code
code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox models an in-memory workspace and a rigged verdict layer; it never runs agent-written code (sandbox.py docstring + run_tests returns canned verdicts).
code_only_features.justification_quote: It deliberately does NOT execute arbitrary agent-written code on the host... This keeps the harness safe (sandbox.py)
